detail: To introduce undergraduate level research planning in preparation for the undergraduate dissertation, possible undergraduate research experience, and to lay the foundation for possible graduate school entry.
schedule:
Week 1: Introduction
Contents of the course. Assessments.
Interest-driven research. Research Ethics. Purposes Statements.

Week 2: Literature Reviews
From Purpose Statements to Research Question(s).
Group Work: critique draft purpose statements.

Week 3: State of the Art, Frontiers of Knowledge.
Literature Reviews, Annotated Bibliographies.
Hypotheses and Intentions.
Group Work: critique draft research questions.

Week 4: Refining research questions and hypotheses: Capacity, Capability.
Resources: time, expertise, access, consumables.
Group Work: critique draft annotated bibliography

Week 5: Planning Research Projects
Resource identification, scheduling of resource uses, risk identification and amelioration/
mitigation.
Group Work: critique draft annotated bibliography (again)

Week 6: Executing Research Plans: No plan survives contact with the enemy.
Group work: discuss draft research plans

Week 7: Stop Working and Start Thinking: Real Research.
Group Work: critique draft research plans
methods:
In-person lectures (all sessions)

In-class group work
evaluation:
While students are allocated to groups for group-work within class, and in the hope that this will also provide mutual support outside class-time, all assessments in this course are individual.

Research Purpose Statement (25%)
A 300–500 word document, with up to five references, explaining the basic reason that this research should be done. This should focus on the expected outcomes of the research, including some reference to the benefit to society that would accrue if the research were to be undertaken.

Research Question(s) Statement (25%)
A 150-300 word document, with no references, describing the specific questions that the research would attempt to answer.

Annotated Bibliography (25%)
A 500–1200 word document explaining between three and five key references and their relationship to the proposed research. For sample annotated bibliographies see the Purdue University guide (https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/general_writing/common_writing_assignments/annotated_bibliographies/annotated_bibliography_samples.html). Note that this submission should use the Harvard referencing style although those samples cover other styles.

Full Research Plan (25%)
A document of up to 3000 words, with references, that includes revised versions of the earlier submissions together with specific hypotheses or intentions, a research plan describing the resources needed to carry out the proposed research as well as a schedule and a risk register with ameliorations.
notes:
Students will understand the differences between research purposes, research questions, research hypotheses (science/social science) and research intentions (social science/humanities).

Students will be able to perform limited but focussed literature searches and reviews, and produce annotated bibliographies as a foundation on which to build literature reviews for dissertations/papers.

Students will be able to produce a basic plan for a project to answer research questions and achieve research purposes.

This is an exercise and while students are free to use all or part of the research plan produced in this course for their graduation thesis, there is no requirement for it to be connected in any way.

detail:
This course is designed for students at the advanced level.
The world today is full of important global challenges. The aim of this course is to discuss solutions to global issues in a forum where students from different countries of the world, who are responsible for the future of the planet. Through the class activities, students will develop creative and critical thinking, socio-cultural knowledge, and academic language through discussion on social issues, especially on global ones. A strong focus will be put on how you can develop sub-questions from a single essential question, and answer your own question by integrating ideas and information from multiple texts. In the process, students are expected to develop higher-order thinking, such as reasoning, comparison, abstraction, concretization, and analysis, and develop creative and critical thinking for problem-solving. For this purpose, intensive listening and reading with related activities are also provided to develop skills in integrating ideas and information from multiple texts. The covered topics may include 'Arts and Humanity', 'Disparity and Poverty', and 'Technology and Society'.
By the end of the course, students are expected to be able to :
1) creating various sub-questions from a simple essential question
2) sort out and evaluate questions to set up a good question to research
3) read academic prose critically
4) be engaged in group discussions
5) conduct a small independent research
6) give an academic presentation
7) write a short essay to answer a question
8) reflect and evaluate their own academic work

detail:
This course is designed for students at the elementary level. In this course, students will proceed with their learning individually and autonomously using various resources with peer and instructor’s advice. General simultaneous group teaching will not be conducted for most of the course since the objectives and content of learning will vary by student. Students are expected to be positively and autonomously engaged in their own learning, bearing in mind that those who learn are students themselves.

Specifically, by the end of the course, students are expected to be able to
1) establish their own learning goals and objectives by understanding their own situation, identifying their own problems and needs, and considering what kind of Japanese language use are necessary for them.
2) understand their own suitable learning style by thinking and trying different learning methods upon their needs.
3) master the ability to manage their own learning.
4) improve their Japanese by concentrating on their weak or favorite area of learning.
schedule:
The basic structure of this course is as follows.

At the beginning of the course:
1) Set the goal of learning.
2) Choose a learning method.
3) Create a learning plan.
4) Create an evaluation plan

During the course:
5) Proceed with individual learning.
6) Take feedback from the peers and the instructor.
7) Monitor and manage the learning process.

At the end of the course:
8) Check the learning products, reflect learning process/outcomes and evaluate them.

Each student's content of learning can be changed during the course according to the conference with the instructor; however, students manage their learning themselves in the end.

Volunteer class visitors may also join the class depending on the content of learning. Possible physical resources are published learning materials, books, dictionaries, newspapers, magazines, videos, CDs, online software tools, and so forth. Materials and persons outside the classroom may also be resources. For learning Kanji, the instructor is ready to provide information on resources.

detail:
This course is designed for advanced students (L6-LS).

The course will help students learn the academic Japanese necessary for college life in a comprehensive manner. Through the integrative use of the Japanese language (listening, reading, speaking, and writing), students will not only develop academic language skills but also gain insights into themselves in relation to Japan and the globalized world, particularly in the context of career development. The course will provide fundamental training in analytical reading, discussion, presentation, interviewing and academic writing, focusing on essential topics and issues that students face in the present and near future. Classroom activities are primarily based on collaborative learning, such as group work and peer review, enabling students to develop dialogic competence and reflect on their language use and perspectives.

Specifically, by the end of the course, students are expected to be able to

1)Analytically read semi-academic texts or other course materials related to current issues in working in Japan or a global society.
2)Precisely conduct interviews and execute related activities.
3)Write well-structured essays that cite trustworthy sources.
4)Increase vocabulary and expressions necessary for academic contexts.
5)Develop collaborative competence.
6)Develop reflexivity about their language use and perspectives on their academic lives and careers, and express these through presentations and writing.

category: L(言語・コミュニケーション)
detail:
【授業の概要】
この授業は、アカデミックな場面における口頭表現の運用能力を高めることを目的とする。大学生活において求められる待遇表現を適切に用いることに加え、あらたまった場面で必要とされる日本語の表現スタイルに着目し、相手との関係性、相手にかかる負担のレベル、話し手自身の立場や状況を踏まえた方略的な会話の進め方を学ぶ。授業では、敬語の「正しさ」や「正確さ」そのものよりも、待遇表現を用いることにより会話の目的を達成し、上下関係を含む相手との位置づけや心理的距離を調整する力の操法を重視する。あらかじめ準備された会話の再現ではなく、その場の状況に応じて即時的に対応するタスクや、履修者が抱く疑問の解消につながる意見交換の機会を積極的に設ける。必要に応じて、メール、口頭発表、研究調査に関する依頼文など、書き言葉における待遇表現についても指導、添削を行う。

【授業の到達目標】
・日本語の社会文化的特徴を批判的にとらえることができる。
・多言語・多文化と比較しながら、日本語の社会文化的特徴や疑問点、納得できない点などについて自身の見解を述べることができる。
schedule:
第1回 ガイダンス、履修者のニーズ分析、敬語コミュニケーション場面で困った経験や困難な点を共有する
第2回 初対面のコミュニケーション
第3回 上下関係のある場面①大学内
第4回 上下関係のある場面②大学外
第5回 対等だがやや距離のある関係性
第6回 初対面、知人だが距離がある、親しい関係、上下関係のある関係のある人々が混在する場面
第7回 口頭パフォーマンス(ロールプレイ)、ふりかえり

※第2回から第6回までは、上記の人間関係にかかわる場面とともに以下の会話の内容と目的について学習する、
「紹介する」「伝言を伝える/受ける」「訪問する、相談する、辞去を伝える」「依頼をする、依頼を受ける/断る」「報告する、お礼を伝える」「ほめる/ほめられる」など、履修者のニーズに応じて学習内容を決定する。これらの会話の内容と目的にもとづき、授業では関係性や場面を考慮した会話の作成、ロールプレイ、モデル会話との比較分析、討論、ふりかえりと質疑応答などを行う。

※履修者の興味により、内容が前後したり変更したりする可能性がある。
methods: 口頭でのやり取り(対話、ロールプレイ等)、ディスカッション、グループワークなど。
evaluation: 積極的に授業に取り組む姿勢を最重視する。加えて、討論の参加姿勢と口頭パフォーマンスの成果、即興対応と方略的判断、書き言葉による待遇コミュニケーションを総合的に評価する。評価基準については、ルーブリックを授業内で示す。
notes:
事前学修:各回の場面設定やロールプレイ、話し合いのために場面を具体的に考えておく。その際、①自身の経験や疑問点を簡単に整理し、②使用が可能な表現や言い回しを考える。

事後学修:授業で実際に行ったロールプレイや討論を振り返り、自身が選択した表現の意図を振り返り、別の表現方法の可能性について整理する。必要に応じて、授業内で扱った場面を想定し、自身にとって必要な待遇表現を簡潔にメモする。
class: 1年 文科 理科 2年 文科 理科
guidancePlace: zoomにて実施する。URLは後日UTOLに掲載する予定である。
timeCompensation: 毎回の授業の前後に最大15分程度、学生からの質問や相談を受け付ける時間を設ける。

category: L(言語・コミュニケーション)
detail:
伝わりやすく自然な発音でコミュニケーションができるようになることを目標とする。また、大学での口頭発表等に必要な発音の習得を目指す。授業の概要は以下のとおりである。

(1)リズムやアクセントなどの音韻知識を学びながら、発音練習および活動を行う。
(2)シャドーイング等の練習方法を活用し、発音学習方法を身につける。
(3)自己評価・他者評価によって自分の発音上の問題点を把握し、発音を上達させる。
schedule:

(2)リズム
(3)アクセント①
(4)アクセント②
(5)イントネーション
(6)その他の音声項目
(7)口頭発表
methods:
(1)音韻知識に関する講義
(2)自分の発音を振り返り、問題点の有無を確認する。
(3)問題点を意識化した発音練習を行う。
(4)シャドーイング練習
(5)口頭発表
(6)各授業の最後に復習クイズを行う。
(7)毎回録音課題提出あり。
